name: Sensitivity and Affine Laws for Substitution Crossing Width
statement: Every proper nonempty test satisfies $g(T)\leq s(1_T)$. Equality holds when both $T$ and $T^{\mathrm c}$ are well graded, hence in particular when $T$ is ample. Moreover $g(T)=1$ exactly when $1_T$ is a nonconstant affine Boolean function. For such an affine test and an outer class with both exclusive sections nonempty, $\sigma(C\circ_iT)=\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(T),\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})\}$.
proof: Every free direction of an isolating face is sensitive at its unique concept, proving $g\leq s$. In a well-graded side, the neighbor directions at a concept form a minimum teaching set because a geodesic toward any other concept begins in one of them; taking both sides gives equality. The condition $g=1$ says every square meets the test in zero, two, or four vertices, so parallel edges have equal indicator increments and the indicator is affine over $\mathbb F_2$; the converse is immediate from an active coordinate in every crossing support. The exact ordering-width law then combines the general upper bound with minor-recovery lower bounds.
comments: The parameter $g$ is not pc-minor monotone: deleting zero from the even-parity class in dimension $n\geq3$ gives $g=2$, while projecting one coordinate gives the punctured cube $\{0,1\}^{n-1}\setminus\{0\}$ with $g=n-1$.
